Content: Timing of Presentation of Financial ReportsThe board have moved that all of the source data should be delivered to Campbell Tyson within 10 working days of the end of the financial period. Campbell Tyson should complete the financial statements and have them transmitted to the board members within 15 days of the end of the financial period and the board meeting should be no earlier than 20 working days after the end of the period.Quarter End period information should be supplied in April (for March), July (for June), October (for September) and January (for December).Documents and Reconciliations to be provided by Firstflex to Campbell Tyson are below.If Dee has processed any month end reports during the quarter, the saved reports will be in Q: AA General Info / Office Admin / Month End ReportsTick1.Copies of Bank Statements showing the balance of each account at the end of the quarter. For chq a/c, savings a/c and loans.2.Firstflex Bank Reconciliation reports that match the balances on the bank statements in #1. For chq a/c and savings a/c  print these out of Pronto as part of the Bank Reconciliation process.3.GST Returns processed during the quarter. A one month GST reconciliation needs to be provided if the GST period doesnt align with the quarter end month. Eg for June quarter, GST for the month of June will need to be reconciled on its own as the prior GST Return was for the April  May period, the next one June  July period. Follow the GST Return procedure  document 502.4.Copies of all invoices supporting asset purchases during the quarter. Davinder/Campbell Tyson will provide the depreciation adjustment to make with the aligning journals once the final accounts have been prepared. No need for us to process a Depreciation amount until then.5.Copies of Donation receipts, provide these once per year for the whole year in April,6.Stock Valuation Report. This was printed as part of the month end process. Content: KPIs entered and Saved in Q:\Caths Folder\HOD & Board\HOD Info\Monthly KPIsTo be done and copied into Meetings/HOD Meetings Folder by the first Friday following each month end.These two KPIs are entered on the “FX” sheet of the workbook.DAYS DEBTORS;Find the Net Sales figure of the month report is for.  Needs to be after the Rebate provision accounts have been reconciled and adjusted as part of month end process.  This is found on the “PLBA” Profit and Loss Actual/Budget comparison report out of GL reporting in Pronto.  (Example reports are attached).Divide that figure by the number of days in the month.  This is the Sales per Day figure.Now from the Debtors ATB report (jasper), take the total Debtors balance and deduct GST.  (Example calculations follow this instruction page).Divide the GST excl. debtors total by the daily sales figure.  This is the overall Days Debtors KPI.Corys and Ideal have special terms where they can pay on the 1st of the month 2 months following invoice date.  We do another calculation taking this into account to reflect a more accurate KPI, to calculate this, take the total debtors figure from the ATB again (GST incl.)Deduct Corys and Ideals payments made on the 1st of the month.Deduct the GST from this figure and divide that again by the daily sales figure.  This is the Days Debtors KPI, taking into account Corys and Ideal special terms.Both KPIs are reported for comparison month by month.  Our usual range is between 40  45 days overall and 30  35 days after Corys and Ideal payments are taken into account.  A figure outside these ranges will mean we had customers pay late and is not good for cashflow.FX/PURCHASING;The forward FX Cover section of the page is really a duplicate of the information in the FX Contracts spreadsheet maintained as part of the AP International supplier purchases function.Take the monthly requirements and monthly purchased totals and enter them in the appropriate currency section (i.e. USD, AUD, and EUR).  Copy across the average currencies also.  Now update the graph so that it picks up the current/newly entered figures.  Look up the system rates in Pronto  under Administration tab/System Admin/System codes & messages/Local-Foreign currency maintenance/Currency maintenance/Local-Foreign Currency Maintenance.For the Purchases Graph; skip to the “FX Purchases” sheet in the KPIs workbook  should be next to the FX sheet you are working in.From the Yellowfin Report  “Stock Supplier Orders in NZ$.......” (copy attached), take the totals for each month and copy these into the FX Purchases spreadsheet in the matching month.Enter the FX gain from GL account 12250 in the matching month and then update the graph to include your new figures.

Content: Product code: MGB1Description: Meter BoxTools Required:Caulking GunBackboard Mounting BoxDrillOscillating KnifeRollerScraperRulerHeat GunMETER BOX COMPONENTSMGBLDM (Meter Box Lid Moulding) MBGPC (Meter Box Back Panel)MGBE (Meter Box Base Moulding)Flashing KitFLASHING KIT COMPONENTSFlashing Kit InstructionsPVCANG365 + PVCANG565MGBFLTP + MGBFLBMMeter Erector PackElectrician Pack.ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS for Flashing Kit (MGBFK):Assemble the neutral stud (NEUSTU) in the following order as per the photo below: SCRM625CSB, STADOFF (Standoff Mould), NUTM6B, WASHM6B, WASHM6B, NUTM6B.Make up the electrician pack (ELEPAC) using the following items as per the photo: BAG9, NEUSTA, SCR820PP x 4, SCR812MP X 2Make up the erector pack (EREPAC) using the following items as per the photo:  BAG9 & SCR820PP x 4. Stick the Erector pack label on the outside of the bagCut a 600mm length of tube and seal off one end.To make the Flashing Kitset, place the following items into the tube: 1 x EREPAC, 1 x ELEPAC, 2 x PVCANG365, 2 x PVCAND565, 2 x MGBFLTP, 2 x MGBFLBM, 1 X MGB Instruction Set. Seal the tube.ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS for Meter Box Lid (MGBLID):Look for any distortions in the lid moulding before continuing. Place any distorted lids to one side and continue with the rest. Content: Operational FeaturesThe ET30 meter is a 30amp coin or token operated electronic timer. Is provides secure, reliable and affordable timing metering solutions for switching up to 30 amps. Standard features include credit save facility, resettable and non-resettable coin counter, dual or single coin operation and the time period may be set in minutes and seconds or hours and minutes. An optional override key is available.Main featuresThe 4 digit 7 segment display, in conjunction with the hidden programming buttons is used to program the ET30, as well as showing the time remaining and mode of operation (figure 4)The coin entry inserts tokens or coins.The optional key override switch turns the timer output on permanently.Access for wiring is via the cover lock (see Wiring).Cash box holding 100 coins.Hidden programming buttons (Programming credit, page 3)Preparation for programmingUnlock and remove cash drawer (this needs to be left out while programming)Unlock the front cover of the meter and lift upwards slightly and away from the wall bracket (see Figure 2).  Unplug the cover ribbon cable lead from the wall bracket and remove cover.For Coin Operation see below, for Token Operation go to Wiring sectionCoin OperationUnscrew clear plastic cover and remove, (2 screws) Unscrew black plastic cover and remove, (2 screws)Discard the short screw as it will no longer be required.Remove L2 label and the small plastic strip behind it.  This can be discarded.Remove the plastic guide rail.Remove the token adaptor plate and replace with a coin adaptor plate, either ET30CK1.00 (for $1 coins) or ET30CK 50 (for 50cent coins).Reassemble black plastic cover & clear plastic cover. Content: Live Testing of 230V Electrical Products ProcedureScope: Testing 230V electrical products.Requirements:RCBO test rig (Test & Tag up to date)QUICKTEST rig2 People (1 Person must have previous testing experience) Details:First identify if the device needs live testing. If not, use an alternative method for instance the PAT testerWhen live testing needs to be carried out, the buddy system detailed below needs to be followed.2 people need to be present during a testing procedureOne being the tester the other being the observerThe observers role is to limit any distractions directed towards the tester whilst in the middle of testing. They are also there to bring to the attention of the tester any potential hazard that may occur while carrying out testingIf testing starts to exceed 10 minutes, please advise the Electrical Production Manager ASAPThe observer and the tester are to report any NEAR MISS to the Electrical Production Manager immediately and fill out the appropriate formsRCBO Testing ProcedureCheck RCBO test rig for an up to date Test & Tag label and for any obvious damageConnect white 3-pin 10A plug into a power outlet and switch it on/Open the cover and switch the RCBO upwards to the ON position/Press the TEST button on the RCBO and check that the RCBO switches back to the OFF position before continuing/Check for any other potential hazards or damage to the product requiring a test before plugging it into one of the below sockets/Switch the RCBO to the ON position to begin testing the product/Proceed to test the live device with caution and isolate the product if found to be faultyTesting with live leads (QUICKTEST)Details:When testing with live leads always use the QUICKTEST isolation unitThe QUICKTEST unit can be plugged into the above RCBO jig (in series) to add an extra layer of protection while testingThe QUICKTEST will liven the 3 output terminals when the black lid is closedQUICKTEST Testing ProcedurePlug the power inlet for METREL into the RCBO test rigPlug the white QUICKTEST plug into the METREL tester/Connect the live lead to the item to be tested/Open up the QUICKTEST unit and connect your live lead to the 3 terminals as below. Content: Worksite Hazard and Incident Management:1. The premises of Firstflex are to be inspected on a monthly basis for any hazards, including, but not limited to: potential trip, slip and fall hazards, electrical, height safety and fire compliance including egresses and exits [See Appendix 13  Site Inspection Form]2. Aisle Inspection to be carried out in the warehouse every Wednesday with inspection report emailed to all H&S   team members.3. Prior to commencement of any significant work, hazards and potential hazards are discussed, with procedures being adopted and documented to mitigate these hazards.  This includes:3.1. Staff being advised of all safety requirements.  These will include any that are specific to a particular site.3.2. Staff being advised of all personal protective equipment and clothing requirements.3.3. Personal protective equipment is provided to all employees and all employees are trained in its use.4. Updates on safety requirements for all mechanical engineering staff, are carried out at toolbox meetings which are conducted prior to work starting and as issues arise.5. Staff, contractors and other visitors are briefed and also alerted to site specific hazards and to general safety requirements through visual signage erected on site.6. Areas where machinery is being used should be restricted to authorised personnel only.  Appropriate signage and hazard tape used where appropriate.7. Visitors to the workshop must wear a high visibility vest.Health & Safety MeetingsHealth & Safety team meetings are held bi-monthly.   Meetings are compulsory for key staff and a minimum of one management representative must be present.  The meeting agenda includes:? Updates to Firstflexs Health & Safety policies and procedures,? Accident incident review,? Hazard Management, including site specific issues,? Key issues from toolbox meetings,? Re-Occurring Incidents,? Off-site issues if any; and? Staff concerns and suggestions in regard to health & safety.Procedures will be amended and manual documentation will be updated where required as a result of outcomes of the monthly health & safety meetings.Staff are further notified through a group meeting or hard copy memo of any changes or updates to Firstflex Cables Health & Safety policies and procedures and associated changes to Health & Safety documentation.Toolbox MeetingsHealth & safety is also an important part of onsite toolbox meetings.  At toolbox meetings a review of accidents/ incidents, hazards and general staff concerns are covered.  In the same manner as above, procedures are amended and manual documentation is updated where required.Toolbox meetings can be a regular scheduled occurrence if the industry or business requires this approach or a more informal process (in addition to the scheduled health & safety meeting) used whenever the team discusses health & safety issues.The specific function of the toolbox meeting is to assist with health & safety specific to the current work that team members are working on.  During this meeting, the team will review, plan and implement and actions relating to health & safety including, but not limited to the following:? Accidents/ incidents, including serious harm, near misses, and associated trends? Regular site inspections,? Hazard assessments, including new hazards and a review of the hazard register,? Personal protective equipment,? Contractor work, including any new contractors that have come onto site,? Any other issues arising from the work being performed, and? Health & Safety training where required,? Progress of work and specific tasks,? Health & Safety, specifically hazards, accidents/ incidents and PPE requirements; and? Mitigation of risks identified in the aboveAll of the above is recorded in the toolbox meeting minutes (Appendix 6.1) and any information that is relevant to either the site or staff in general, is communicated via general memorandum or staff email.  Appropriate action is taken immediately if required and review takes place at the next toolbox or health & safety meeting.Key issues from toolbox meetings should be reported in the next Health & Safety Meeting.Refer to Firstflex Health and Safety Manual for full dutiesOriginal Copy approved byH&S___________________GM______________________MD_______________________

Content: Technical Explanation of the Pricing SheetsWhat Does It Do?The 4-supplier template takes the pricing sheets from the suppliers and uses them to update Pronto according to certain rules.Formatting the Data for ProntoFirst, it creates a format that matches the raw data so the results sheet is, in essence, a copy of that raw data, ready to upload back into the same screen.This is seen in column A, which directly pulls the data:='raw pronto'!A2Handling Blank ValuesSome columns need to return blanks instead of zeros:=IF('raw pronto'!B2=0,"",'raw pronto'!B2)Supplier 1 Code Handling for X ArticlesAny X article should use the supplier of the normal article. X codes represent the same product but are separated to avoid interfering with reordering.=IF(IF(LEFT(A2,1)="X",'raw pronto'!J2,VLOOKUP(MID(A2,1,99),'raw pronto'!A:J,10,FALSE))=0,"",IF(LEFT(A2,1)="X",'raw pronto'!J2,VLOOKUP(MID(A2,1,99),'raw pronto'!A:J,10,FALSE)))Looking Up the Supplier and Standardizing X or ASSY ArticlesThe supplier is identified, and then the article is found on the vendor sheets. If it is an X article or an ASSY article, the standard (non-X) article is found.If this formula is too complex, a helper worksheet could be used to combine data from each vendor, along with a helper column that assigns the standard article for every item.=LET( lookupValue, IF( LEFT($A2,1)="X", RIGHT($A2, LEN($A2) - 1), IF(RIGHT($A2,4)="ASSY", LEFT($A2, LEN($A2) - 4), $A2) ), result, IF( J2="HENRYCAB", IF(COUNTIF('raw HC'!$A:$A, lookupValue) > 0, VLOOKUP(lookupValue, 'raw HC'!$A:$M, 11, FALSE), 0), IF( J2="RAMRATNA", IF(COUNTIF('raw RR'!$A:$A, lookupValue) > 0, VLOOKUP(lookupValue, 'raw RR'!$A:$N, 11, FALSE), 0), IF( J2="DOMINION", IF(COUNTIF('raw DC'!$A:$A, lookupValue) > 0, VLOOKUP(lookupValue, 'raw DC'!$A:$Z, 9, FALSE), 0), IF( J2="TKDKABEL", IF(COUNTIF('raw TKD'!$A:$A, lookupValue) > 0, VLOOKUP(lookupValue, 'raw TKD'!$A:$O, 9, FALSE)/1000, 0), VLOOKUP($A2, 'raw pronto'!$A:$O, 15, FALSE) ) ) ) ), IFERROR(ROUND(result, 4), 0))This process repeats for Supplier 2 and Supplier 3.Looking Up TKD Part NumbersOn the TKD sheet, the system looks up internal part numbers on the TKD codes sheet. This is a query that can be refreshed.=IFERROR(VLOOKUP([@[TKD Part Number (txt)]]&"",'TKD codes'!E:F,2,FALSE),"")Formatting Codes to Match TKD's FormatThe system converts internal codes to match the TKD format by trimming and removing unnecessary parts:=LEFT(B2, FIND(" ", B2 & " ") - 1)Ensuring internal codes are properly trimmed:=TRIM([@[stock_code]])White bookSimialrly to the last sheet this brings the raw data from pronto onto a front sheetFormulas like this=Data!AJ1And converts the current buy price and currency rate to a replacement cost=IF(F2=0,"",(F2/H2 (1+I2%) (1+J2%)))If it is an X article it pulls the trade price of th non X article=IF(LEFT(A2,1)="X",0,Data!AE1)It looks up rebate from the rebate sheet=IFERROR(VLOOKUP(C3,Rebate!A:B,2,FALSE),"")Column Y will have the final results in it but it needs to initially present us with the current listed prices so it gives us prices from the pronto sheet(data) and if it is an x article it looks up the non x articles data (as that wouldnt have list proices)=IFERROR(IF(AND(LEFT(A4,1)="X",Data!Y3=0),XLOOKUP(MID(A4,2,99)&W4,Data!A:A&Data!W:W,Data!$Y:$Y,"",0),Data!Y3),0)Now BB onwards we aggregate stock by the products stock brand / genericBB looks up the generic=IFERROR(VLOOKUP(A2,generics!$C:$D,2,FALSE),A2)We do the sum if based on the generic to give the numbers that will calculate aversge costs=IFERROR(IF(BB5="","",SUMIF(BB:BB,BB5,BC:BC)),"")Calculate the cost average=IFERROR(IF(LEFT(A5,1)="X",IF(BB4=BB5,BF4,IFERROR(INDEX(BD:BD,MATCH(MID(A5,2,99),A:A,FALSE))/INDEX(BE:BE,MATCH(MID(A5,2,99),A:A,FALSE)),"")),IF(BB4=BB5,BF4,IFERROR(BD5/BE5,""))),"")Now we calculate price tiers based on the minimum margin (AR) the cost (BF) and slowly increasing it and defaulting to the replacement if there is nothing with tiers based on how many price steps there are (BN)=IFERROR($BF6/(1-($AR6)/100),IFERROR(K6/(1-($AR6)/100),""))=IFERROR($BF4/(1-($AR4+2 $BN4)/100),IFERROR(K4/(1-($AR4+2 $BN4)/100),""))I need to know the no of unpublished items so I know how many teirs are unpublished, unpublished is over 4999=IF(AND(A2=A1,D2=D1,W1>4999),BW1,IF(W2>4999,COUNTIFS($A:$A,A2,$D:$D,D2)-BV2+1,""))I assign a minimum grade (looking it up on the minimum price sheet=IFERROR(VLOOKUP(CG2,'Minimum Price'!$A$1:$B$12,2,FALSE),"")And calculate a floor for the product based on preplacement cost=IFERROR(K2 1/(1-VLOOKUP(CG2,'Minimum Price'!$A$1:$B$35,2,FALSE)),"")And calculate a max of that to get it at the generic level=IF(BB2="","",MAXIFS($CD$2:$CD$20000,$BB$2:$BB$20000,BB2))And put it all together in the final price=IFERROR(ROUND(IF(Y2+0=0,"",IF(BO2=0,Y2,IF(BW2="",Y2,MAX(MIN(CE2,IF(A2=A1,CC1,Y2)),IF(CA2="N",OFFSET(BO2,0,COUNTIFS($A:$A,A2,$D:$D,D2)-BV2),IF(AND(CC1<BO2,A2=A1,D2=D1),CC1,CB2)))))),2),"")That value is them pasted to the Y column and we upload the price file

Content: How to release/resume a Suspended AP Invoice batch/To release a suspended AP batch, go to Accounts payable, Supplier Transactions, Additional Supplier Transactions, Resume Suspended Supplier InvoiceThe screen will be blank, but select “In Progress”The following screen pops up;/Now select “Suspend”The following screen pops up;/If the batch looks to be the one youre needing released, put a Y in the box, then Enter.Now press ESCClick on Select, then OKThe next screen takes you straight into the batch where you were last entering a transaction, the screen looks blank but press ESC to take you out of the last entry and then the rest of your batch will appear above that line.If all looks ok as you left it, find where your last entry was to see what invoices still need entering, check your payment due dates etc and then Post the batch.If you want to make sure youve captured everything correctly, check the entries in the supplier to see that theyve posted.

Content: Objective:  To effectively screen new product opportunities to decide if they are worth introducing to the product mix.Action Steps:Ask the following screening questions about the product, to determine where it fits on a scale from 1 being definitely NO and 5 being definitely YES.REAL - Is there a real market for this product? Questions below focus on the Market.Screening QuestionsCommentsScale 1 to 5Is there a need or desire for the product?Can the customer buy it direct?Is the size of the potential market adequate?Will the customer buy the product?Are there subjective barriers to purchasing it?Is there a clear concept?Can the product be made?Could it be created with available technology and materials, or would it require a breakthrough of some sort?If it can be created, can it be produced and delivered cost effectively or would it be so expensive that potential customers would shun it?Will the final product satisfy the market?WIN  Can we gain and maintain a competitive edge? Questions below focus on being competitiveScreening QuestionsCommentsScale 1 to 5Can the product be competitive?Are there any features and benefits?Does it have a competitive advantage?Can someone elses offering provide customers with the same results or benefits?Can the advantage be sustained?How will competitors respond?If we were going to attack our own product, what vulnerabilities would we find?  How can we reduce them?Would the product survive a sustained price war?Can our company be competitive?Do we have superior resources?Do we have appropriate management?Does the Company have direct or related experience with the market?Are the Companys development-process and skills appropriate for the scale and complexity of the project?Does the project both fit the company culture and have a suitable champion?Can we understand and respond to the market?WORTH IT  Will the expected payoff be worth the risks involved? Questions below focus on risks vs. payoffs.Screening QuestionsCommentsScale 1 to 5Will the product be profitable at an acceptable risk?Are the forecasted returns greater than costs?Are risks acceptable?Effort / Return RatioHow will small changes in price, market share, and launch timing affect cash flows and break-even points?Does launching the product make strategic sense?Does the product or service fit our overall growth strategy?Will it enhance the companys capabilities by for example, driving expansion of manufacturing, human capital, logistics, or other functions?Will it have a positive or negative impact on brand equity?Will it cannibalize or improve sales of the companys existing products?Will it enhance or harm relationships with stakeholders?Does the project create opportunities for follow-on business or new markets that would not be possible otherwise?Is the product suitable for its intended environment e.g. UV, chemicals etc. Has it been used by other distributors overseas, what was their feedback. Will the product be perceived as low, mid, or high end? Is it an old copy, good mid-range  or new and innovativeOutcome from screening exercise / decision to proceed or not.38 QuestionsTotal score out of a possible 190 =% = Total score Divided by 190 x 100 =
Summary: Evaluation checklist for reviewing and approving new product introductions.

Content: There are 2 types of invoices - a Tax Disbursement Invoice (GST) and a Tax invoice GST is charged on the Tax Disbursement invoice and ALWAYS goes with the customs certificateRefer to the Shipment Charges spreadsheet (document 693P) to colour code the chargesThe Tax Disbursement invoice usually has an Admin Fee and an entry feeCheck the GST amount on Tax Disbursement Invoice Select Purchase Orders ( Shipment Processing ( Maintain Shipment detailsPress FindType in the SH numberEnter - the shipment details will showLook at the value in the foreign currency (USD,EURO etc)Locate the exchange rate used on the customs certificateDivide the foreign value by the exchange rate on the custom cert e.g. 245231.38 ÷ 0.63Check the value on your calculator and compare it to the Subtotal on your Tax disbursement invoiceIf the amount on the calculator is close to the subtotal, it is acceptable. What happens when the amounts differ??Put an approved for payment stamp on bottom line with small signaturePut shipment number in the right hand corner as a reference for the accounts teamOn the Tax Invoice / Tax Disbursement Invoice, highlight the charges with their appropriate colour  refer to document 693P for the colour code chart.Once all charges are colour coded, add up the totals for each colour.Write the category and total for each colour (e.g. Admin Fee $20.00) as per the following examples.
Summary: Instructions for reviewing and approving tax invoices from Tristar.

Content: Creating the Commercial Invoice Ensure you have weight and dimensions of the item you are sending before starting.Q: Drive \ AA General Info \ Commercial Invoices & Proforma InvoiceSelect the supplier you are sending goods toClick on date modified to put all the invoices in date created order.Click into the most recent commercial invoice to open it.Click File.Click Save As.Click Browse - it should come up where all the other invoices for that supplier are saved.Save as a new invoice and change the date at the end to todays date.Update the following fields:Date of Export:enter todays date.International Waybill No:enter the Toll Air Waybill NumberFull Description of Goods:specifically what you are sending.Quantity: the quantity being sentUnit: the unit measure e.g. metre, each etc. Unit Value:the buy price for that item.Total Weight:the total weight of all goods being sent.Dimensions:the total cubic metres or dimensions of all goods being sent.Date:enter todays date (bottom right corner).SavePrint 3 x copies on Firstflex letterheadGet the sender of the goods to sign each of the 3 original copies.Photocopy 1 of the originals for our ref.Completing the Toll Airway Bill  see example belowBox 1:Check the AWB# matches that on the commercial invoice you created.Box 2:Tick Charge Sender.Box 4:Sign write todays date.Box 5:Write the company name, address, city, country, postcode and phone number.Box 7:Tick Permanent Export and Charge Sender.Box 8:Service Type = Economy Door to Door.Description of Contents = description of goods being sent e.g. Electrical Goods (Samples)Size & Weight = write the total quantity, weight and dimensionsPhotocopy the completed Airway Bill for our reference.Packing and distributing the goods Put a lock re-sealable bag on the box. If you are using a satchel, there is already one provided.Put the original AWB and the 3 original commercial invoices in the lock re-sealable bag on the box or satchel.If on the box, tape down all sides of the lock re-sealable bag.Write in vivid clearly on the box or satchel the WB# and the ultimate destination.Ring Toll on 0800 231531 and book a collection.Write down the booking ref and track until goods have arrived at the destination.
Summary: Detailed steps for exporting goods, including documentation and compliance checks.

Content: Receiving incoming callsInternal salesTechnical support/quotesFred / Rissie / Ali / Greg / Shane / Doug / BDM ManagersDan, Jimmy, Marty, Bruce (Technical Support)If the phone has rung more than 3 TIMES, it is the responsibility of all office employees to answer it.  If you are already on a call, you may have to put your caller on hold to answer the incoming call.When answering an incoming call the standard greeting is:                    “Welcome to Firstflex ………………… speaking.”If the caller asks for a staff member by name, say: “I will check if____is available, who can I say is calling?”If the caller asks for a staff member by name but that person is busy/unavailable/out of the office, TELL the caller what time/day that particular person is due back.  Then:Ask the caller if someone else in sales can help.Offer to take a message and have the particular person return their call when they are available/back in the office.Offer the staff members mobile number only if asked for but advise first if person is unavailable due to being in a meeting and give time details for when they will be available. Do not give out personal mobile phone numbers.If you are unsure which department the caller needs to talk to, try the General Manager or the Sales Manager.Any request to answer surveys or request for privileged company information are to be directed to the Managing Director.  If the Managing Director is unavailable then the Sales & Marketing Director will take the call and deal with it in an appropriate manner.Transferring Calls When talking to a customer, press the Transfer keyDial the extension to transfer to, then select the type of transfer  BlindTrnf or AttTrnf BlindTrnf: The call is transferred immediately, so just hang up. AttTrnf: This gives you a chance to speak to the person you are transferring to.  Once you have announced the caller, just hang up.If the person you are transferring to doesnt want the call he / she can hang up and the call comes back to you.Putting Calls on Hold Press the Hold (pause) button at the lower right side of the phone.To take the caller off hold, press resume button on screen

Content: New customer account opening requirements and approvals:1. Complete Credit Application Form (Document 342) and New Customer Details Form (Document 344)2. Content: The purpose of the Industrial Stock Profile (ISP) is to get stock onto the customers shelf. The ISP and its contents is only a guide as to what we deem as our Industrial cables that would be a good industrial stock profile in any electrical wholesaler. You can customize the offer as you see fit, or if there is a demand for other products. Analyze sales for the branch and identify what products they regularly buy but dont actually stock. Present your findings to the decision makers at the branch. This process will show that you are adding value to their business and builds higher levels or trust and skill.Identify which branch you want to do the ISP for.Print a manual page ISP Pronto / Jasper reporting / Login / Reports / Firstflex / Invoiced Sales / Industrial Stock Profile/ Enter Territory / Enter Branch / Apply / Export PDF / PrintDo a manual stock inventory at the branch or get a printout from them of what Firstflex stocks they carry.Enter the ISP into Insightly. Generate Stock Group Sales Comparison  (Cust Grp Comparison) ReportLog in to YellowfinBrowse / Firstflex Reports / Non-Dashboard Sales Click on Marketing Group Sales Comparison (cust group comparison) FFL vs ERXIn the Report Period field, enter the start and end dates you would like for the report. Choose Marketing Group-Customer Sales Comparison-Choose Customer Group of your choiceChoose CustomerFrom here you can see and analyze overall sales for the timeframes you have chosen you can also drill down from overall series data to specific products within that seriesFrom here you will be able to compare what the branch actually stocks with the actual sales in the chosen period, look for patterns of regular sales of the same productsTo export this data into a excel spreadsheet press the arrow up icon-Export to XLSX-Export-Open-Enable Editing-Delete columns that are not needed or is sensitive information that is NOT to be given to customers e.g. column GP%. File Name: 802W Fork Lift Batteries Top Up Procedure.docx
Content: Important Notes:Lower fluid levels may reduce the battery capacity and reduce the service life of the battery.Higher liquid levels may lead to electrolyte overflow when charging, which may cause corrosion to the battery compartment or the vehicle.The hoists should be put on charge every Fridays at the end of the day so they are ready to be topped up on Monday morning.Do not tip the liquid content from the bucket onto the concrete as it will leave a permanent acid stain.PPE gear, gloves and glasses must be worn at all times when using the battery water refill equipment.Before you begin check the condition of the cable leads, cells and especially dry acid build-up.Report any issues to the Warehouse Manager.If the red buoy is not floating, top up the cells with distilled water from the bucket.Correct Water Level: The white line should just be showing. This is also visible through the transparent filler caps. Top up the battery cells using the jug and funnel or the hand pump.If you over fill or find the cells are already over filled, you must remove the excess water.Wrong Water Level: The white line on the buoy is fully showing.Excess battery water must be sucked out with the hand pump and put back into the distilled water bucket.

Content: Cable InformationAll cable leaving the premises must have a brand / size / voltage embossed or printed on the cable unless on the exceptions list below: SIHF / SICY HCT / HCS / HCSF / HCTCY / HCSCY / HCTF / HCM / HCMHF / HCMHFX / HCK6HCY / HCP / HCG3 / HCE3 / HCG1 / HC3CV7CMS / MTS / MBS / MFE / MTRAll extra low voltage cables which are wound onto drums must not leave the premises without a “Caution not suitable for mains connection E.L.V. only” sticker placed on the drum. Dan to check thisAll cable must be meter marked if over 30 metres in length, unless otherwise stated. All cables that are metre marked must have a start and finish length recorded on the curve label. Cables are to be printed in black only. How to wind and package cable:Find an appropriate drum to suit the type of cable to be wound off: Ensure the bending radius of the cable suits the bending radius on the drum. Put multi core, screened and SWA cables on drums with big bores to prevent breakage or on hand winder then wrap with plastic wrap. Ignoring the bending radius on SWA cables will cause severe defects to the cable once it is pulled off the drum.Once the drum is mounted onto the cable winder, pull the cable through the metre mark counter and secure it tightly to the drum.  Wind the cable on to the drum.If cable is being printed be careful on speed so as not to distort printing.Cable rolls must not exceed the outer flange diameter of the cable reel.Short lengths of small cable can be pulled manually through meter counter.Use the hand winder for short lengths of larger cables and SWA.  Cut off the desired amount, tie plastic wrap to end of the cable and wrap around 3 -4 times.If cable is meter marked, always cut on the meter marks (as long as meter marks are correct and accurate).If rolling 20m or less of cable, shrink wrap the cable, then tape or cable tie the ends. If the hand roll is small, pack it into a suitably sized box. How to pick accessories and non-lot tracked cable:Go to the allocated bin location displayed on the PICKING SLIP and pick corresponding components with order.  Use separate plastic bags for each different product and label each bag. Conduit Lengths must be in manageable weight bundles, securely taped together with address secured onto bundle with plastic wrap. All conduit lengths are sent via Mainfreight, Transauck and Owens (unless collected).  Packing slip to be stuck and taped on with clear tape. Galvanised FittingsPack smaller conduit fittings into separate plastic bags for every different product, packed well (not loose) and boxed.  The Distribution Manager (or 2IC) will advise whether boxed conduit fittings or other boxed accessories should be attached to the conduit or not for truck freight. All galvanised fittings and accessories must always be rust free when dispatched.To clean fittings before dispatch, use the wire brush nozzles to remove any rust (nozzles are located on the work bench).Flexible Conduit (metal or PVC)Place flexible conduit on metre marked floor or pull it carefully through the meter counter and cut to ordered length.Cut by grabbing with both hands and snapping, then snip the conduit between the 2 breaks.If flexible conduit is PVC coated (GFCP) or GFCLT, you will need to neatly cut the PVC with a knife first.Pack in the appropriate bag, box or on a reel.Individual Duties:Order Entry: Process the order and put the paperwork in the appropriate tray.Main Picker / Driver:Pick and load up cables behind lifters depending on the urgency of the order. Combined orders - Non-Lot Tracked items to be picked once the cable has been cut. Does the main picker do this?Picker # 2/Accessories: Pick non-tracked orders only and place goods on the packing bench.Winders:Wind and cut the cable, then place on the packing bench to be checked. When a combined order, advise Picker #2 to proceed to the next step.  Is the next step picking accessories?Packer(s)  Bench:Check all items on the packing bench against the picking slip. Ensure you check the item code, colour (if applicable) and quantity so the correct goods are sent.Tick each item on the picking slip as you check and sign the picking slip once checked and correct.Package goods securely, put the packing slip into a packing slip sleeve and attach to the goods.Print an address label and attach to the box(es) and / or drum(s)  see 815W, 816W and 817W.Combined orders to be regularly checked. Once both NON-Tracked and Tracked items come together, checked, packed, made ready for pickup.

Content: Test PreparationSamples will be selected from shipments based on the FirstTest Testing Plan. The plan is located in the following location: Q Drive / FirstTest / Test Plan Cable Series  Insulation & Sheath. There will be changes made to the plan when unplanned testing may be required. This will be updated by the Operations Manager and Test leader.Sample series and sizes will be picked based on the FirstTest Testing Plan, timing of test and the next incoming shipment list that is available from purchasing. Preferably select cable conductors size around 4mm to 6mm.  The Operations manager and Test Leader will pick which cables series and sizes to test. This list must be given to inwards who will cut the samples and amend the Lot numbers. 2mtre samples are required.Print off the Test Report Guide that relates to the series and size to be tested. The plan is located in the following location: Q Drive / FirstTest / Test Reports.Fill out the details at the top of the report that relates to the shipment the samples were taken from.We have a Test Report Guide for each item code. The cable series, size and number of cores will determine how many tests must be completed. Example: MCH7/1.5SWA you will only test two cores, not seven. Once all test values, notes and conclusions are recorded, scan a copy and send it to your email address. Open the PDF document from your email and save it in in the following location: Q Drive / FirstTest / Completed Tests. Use the item code and shipment P/O number as the File Name.Any test that has failed must be reported to the Operations Manager. The corresponding drum must be placed on HOLD in Pronto and a yellow sticker put on the drum. The Operations Manager will contact the manufacturer and advise set steps.Cable Sample Preparation6 samples from the same sheath and/or insulation must be prepared, depending on the test. 3 samples for the aging oven, elongation and tensile test. 3 test samples are required to get a positive result.3 samples for Non aging oven, elongation and tensile test. 3 test samples are required to get a positive result.Refer to AS/NZS1660.2.1 standards for preparation requirements.1 sample of each core must be prepared for the conductor resistance. This sample must be 1.2 meters in length. Refer to Conductor Resistance Test Procedure. 1 sample of the insulation and/or 1 sample from the sheath must be prepared for the Profile Projector. Refer to Cable Profile Projector Test Procedure
